title: A 2% budget usually lands in the middle of a tie
caption: Each bar is the 500 honest programs, ranked from most to least suspicious by one monitor; programs with the same score form one block. Only the top 10% is shown. Blue blocks are audited; the amber block is a tie the budget cuts through, so you audit all of it or none.
notes: Report exact budgets as the main numbers, with the audit-only-above-the-tie numbers and the rate they really audit in an appendix table.
More honest data doesn't fix ties: a 0 to 10 score only ever offers 11 places to cut. It does fix the other problem, that at 500 honest programs a 1% budget rests on just 5 of them.

series.name: Audited
series.renderItem: function (params, api) { var a = api.coord([api.value(0), api.value(2)]); var b = api.coord([api.value(1), api.value(2)]); var h = api.size([0, 1])[1] * 0.6; return {type: 'rect', shape: {x: a[0], y: a[1] - h / 2, width: Math.max(b[0] - a[0], 1), height: h, r: 2}, style: api.style()}; }
